Commentary.Commentary: Welcome back for India's response with the bat. The umpires and players make their way out to the middle. Salman Agha leads his men out as the players of Pakistan scatter throughout the park and take their positions. Abhishek Sharma will partner with Shubman Gill to open for India. We saw the odd ball holding up a bit off the deck in the first innings, and there was a bit of early movement as well. But how much impact will dew make, IF there is any? Let's find out. Shaheen Afridi to bowl the first over, Abhishek to face. But for starters, Shaheen vs Gill will be a very spicy match-up to watch out for. The countdown is over, and here we go...
... THE RUN CHASE ...

Right then, Pakistan have posted a challenging total on the board. And this is the first time, India will be chasing a target as big as this in this Asia Cup. A strong start from Shubman Gill and Abhishek Sharma becomes a non-negotiable for the Indians. Whereas the Pakistan bowlers will be desperate to snag a couple of early wickets to push India on the back foot. It is pretty even-stevens at this point and to know where the scales tilt eventually, do stick around with us as the run chase is on the other side very shortly.

However, cricket is a game of phases and to gain a complete upper hand, one needs to be consistent. Pakistan could not sustain that. 10.3, right after the break, Shivam Dube broke the deadlock for India, and from there, the wheels just came off for Pakistan. The Indian spinners, Kuldeep Yadav and Varun Chakaravarthy, found an opening and just gatecrashed through it, completely choking the run rate. Dube produced another gold by dismissing Farhan on 58, and with that, Pakistan slipped from a very commanding 93/1 to 115/4. From overs 11-15, Pakistan could only score 28 runs, losing three big wickets, without a boundary in that phase. And with an intention to bail their side out of the hole, Agha, Nawaz, and Faheem, with their late cameos, helped Pakistan to post 171.

They say, you can have an off day with the bat, or with the ball as well, but an off day in the field proves really stinging. Abhishek Sharma dropped two catches of Sahibzada Farhan, who looked in an overdrive mode and also sprinkled salt on India's wounds with a blistering fifty. Saim Ayub and Farhan formed a stable partnership of 72 runs, and at that point, Pakistan were looking to finish in excess of 200, with enough wickets in hand and sloggers yet to come to bat.

Pakistan’s concern had often been their slow starts in the Powerplay, but a new opening pair flipped that narrative. Fakhar Zaman looked dangerous before his dismissal sparked plenty of debate. Sahibzada Farhan, after a major reprieve early on, took the bold route of attacking Jasprit Bumrah - and that bravery paid off, unsettling India’s lengths. To make matters worse for India, Kuldeep Yadav put down a sitter off Saim Ayub, and with so much happening, Pakistan made the most of it to finish the Powerplay at 55/1.

After a long, long time, this one has given a proper vibe to an India vs Pakistan game. In all fairness, Pakistan came out much improved with the bat. They bossed the initial phase, but then India sprang back strongly, controlling the middle overs. But it was then followed by a strong finish from the finishers as Pakistan managed to score 42 runs off the last 3 overs. India could have actually restricted them to a total way less than this, had they managed to cling on to easy catches that they grassed through and through.

SIX! Faheem Ashraf manages to apply the finishing touches and Pakistan go beyond 170. Full and wide again from Pandya, Ashraf reaches out and manages to get to the ball. The ball gets sliced and it goes flat, over the leaping fielder at deep backward point for a six. 14 off the final over and Pakistan finish with 171/5 on the board!

Commentary.Commentary: DRINKS BREAK. So far, so good from Pakistan. They have shown a really positive intent from the first ball and have received the rewards for an aggressive approach. Dropping Sahibzada Farhan twice, and Saim Ayub once, India have looked really sloppy in the field and they need to break this partnership as quickly as possible to put a lid on the scoring. However, seemingly, the ball hasn't got enough grip and turn this time around for the spinners and hence, it has made batting look comfortable. Also, attacking India's main man, Jasprit Bumrah early doors proved to be really fruitful for Pakistan. If either of these two blokes bat till the end, 200 is well within reach. With that said, out come the two sets of players and they line up for their respective national anthems. It will be the national anthem of Pakistan first, followed by the Indian national anthem.

PITCH REPORT - Sanjay Manjrekar and Ravi Shastri are pitchside with their analysis. Sanjay says that the decision at the toss has a lot to do with the track record. Shares that it is a dry pitch and reckons that batting later on will become a bit easier even if the dew doesn't come. Ravi details that ball grips in Dubai and the pitch is expected to assist the spinners a lot. Stresses that the batters will have to give themselves some time to settle in, and it will eventually get a bit easier.

India (Playing XI) - Abhishek Sharma, Shubman Gill, Suryakumar Yadav (C), Tilak Varma, Sanju Samson (WK), Shivam Dube, Hardik Pandya, Axar Patel, Kuldeep Yadav, Jasprit Bumrah (In for Arshdeep Singh), and Varun Chakaravarthy (In for Harshit Rana).

Pakistan (Playing XI) - Sahibzada Farhan, Saim Ayub, Fakhar Zaman, Salman Agha (C), Hussain Talat (In for Khushdil Shah), Mohammad Haris (WK), Mohammad Nawaz, Faheem Ashraf (In for Hasan Nawaz), Shaheen Afridi, Haris Rauf, and Abrar Ahmed

The captain of Pakistan, Salman Agha, says they would have bowled first as well. Adds that it is a new game and the mood in the dressing room is pretty normal. Says they just want to play a good brand of cricket. Reckons that the pitch is expected to be a bit on the slower side. Stresses that they look forward to starting well with both bat and ball. In the end, he informs that Hasan Nawaz and Khushdil Shah make way for Hussain Talat and Faheem Ashraf.

India's captain, Suryakumar Yadav, says that they saw a lot of dew last night as well. Mentions that it is just another game for them and they want to enjoy it. TOSS UPDATE - The flip of the coin lands in favor of India and Suryakumar Yadav elects to BOWL first.

In Dubai, one clear trend has stood out in this Asia Cup. The team that controls the Powerplay in the first innings usually ends up with the upper hand. Across the six games so far, including the Sri Lanka vs Bangladesh Super 4 clash, the average first inning Powerplay score has been just 44. Only once has a side crossed fifty, and that came in the previous game. Chasing has not been any easier either. Apart from India, no team has gone at ten runs per over or more in the field restrictions, while India have managed to do it twice. Interestingly, Pakistan have batted first in all three of their league games, while India tried both approaches at least once. India convincingly beat Pakistan at the same venue, exactly a week ago, but will that dominance sustain? We shall find out soon. Toss and team sheets will be up very shortly.

Pakistan’s story, though, has been a bit of a grind. They've found it tough to match the tempo of modern T20 cricket. Across three games in the league stage, their Powerplay returns have been undercooked, averaging 42 and consistently losing early wickets. The most they've managed for the first wicket? Four runs. That lack of a platform has left the middle order exposed and, frankly, under-delivering. The one area that’s held its own is the bowling - Shaheen Afridi and Haris Rauf have done a decent job, and with India’s known vulnerability against left-arm pace, Shaheen’s first couple of overs could set the tone. Oddly enough, while Saim Ayub's bat has gone cold with three ducks, he’s quietly chipped in with the ball, adding value through his 'part-time' spin.

India storm into the knockouts with their sails full and spirits high, having bossed the group stage without a single blemish. They did face an unexpected challenge against Oman a few matches ago, where the bowling came under the microscope, but aside from that, it’s been smooth sailing. Abhishek Sharma has been electric at the top, proving a perfect launchpad for the others, and the middle order has had enough time out in the middle to settle into rhythm. Bowling-wise, India tested their bench strength by bringing in Arshdeep and Harshit, but one of them is likely to sit out to make way for Jasprit Bumrah.

Over the years, these two teams have progressed at enormously different trajectories. World Champions in the inaugural T20 World Cup, and as defending champions now, India carry two global titles and eight Asia Cups in their cabinet. Pakistan’s story is different - just two Asia Cup trophies from sixteen attempts, with their last triumph all the way back in 2012. So while the fans see this as the fiercest battle between two subcontinental giants, the numbers of recent times suggest a rivalry that has leaned heavily one way and more or less has been brittled.

Rivalries make any sport interesting and binge-watch worthy and one of the most talked-about and awaited clashes is back again. It is India vs Pakistan in the second match of the Super 4 in the Asia Cup 2025. We are here at the iconic Dubai International Cricket Stadium and let’s hope this one serves up to its billing. On that note, a literally very warm welcome to everyone joining us. Glad to have you all.
... MATCH DAY ...

We are down to game number two of the Super Four clash, where arch-rivals India and Pakistan lock horns at the Dubai International Stadium. This will be round two of the heavyweight bout, but the first round was a mismatch, as the Men in Blue proved too hot to handle for those in green. There has been plenty of drama ever since that night with the handshake saga, and it does not look like we have seen the last of it. Pakistan, in particular, will need to put all of that behind them before stepping onto the field. Salman Agha and Co. began their campaign with a thumping win over Oman but have since faced tougher challenges. A crushing defeat against India was followed by a hard-fought win over the UAE, where a place in the Super Four was on the line. Since Mike Hesson took over as the head coach, much of the talk has been about playing an aggressive brand of cricket. The slow Dubai surfaces have not allowed Pakistan to express that style, and they have also been guilty of playing too many dot balls, leaving much to be desired in their strike rotation. For two consecutive games, Shaheen Afridi’s late hitting has added respectability to their totals. While Saim Ayub has made his presence felt with the ball, he is yet to open his account with the bat, falling for three ducks in as many innings. Apart from Ayub, the Men in Green will want Sahibzada Farhan, Fakhar Zaman, and Salman Agha to step up against the might of the Indian bowling attack. In their games against Oman and India, Pakistan opted for just one frontline pacer in Shaheen Afridi alongside three specialist spinners, with support from Saim Ayub and Salman Agha. Against the UAE, however, they turned to the raw pace of Haris Rauf, with Sufiyan Muqeem making way. It will be interesting to see which combination they choose this time to contain a strong Indian batting line-up. As far as India are concerned, they have had a flawless run so far. After breezing past the UAE and Pakistan, Suryakumar Yadav's men faced a spirited Omani side that refused to back down. With their spot in the Super Four already secured, India approached the game as an opportunity to give valuable batting time to players who hadn’t featured much. Consequently, Suryakumar chose not to come out to bat and promoted others up the order. The signs of rust were particularly evident in the batting department. Sanju Samson gained valuable time in the middle, while Shubman Gill, Shivam Dube, Axar Patel, and Hardik Pandya had short stays at the crease and would have liked to spend longer. Without Jasprit Bumrah and Varun Chakaravarthy, India experimented with as many as eight bowling options, true to the way they approached the dead rubber. Barring the Oman game, India have generally front-loaded Jasprit Bumrah’s overs in the Powerplay. The spin trio of Kuldeep Yadav, Axar Patel, and Varun Chakaravarthy then take over to inflict the damage in the middle phase. There are doubts over Axar Patel’s participation in this clash after he accidentally banged his head onto the turf while going for a catch against Oman. That could force India to move away from their three-pronged spin attack. Mind you, the Oman game was played in Abu Dhabi, while the rest of India’s upcoming matches will be in Dubai. Although there is not much difference between the two surfaces, it will take time for the Indian batters who haven’t had much time at the crease to adjust. That could become a vulnerability if the top order is dismissed early, and Pakistan will be eager to exploit it. The last time Pakistan defeated India in any format was back in September 2022 in Dubai during the previous edition of the T20 Asia Cup. Since then, the Men in Blue have won all six completed meetings. Can Pakistan finally break the streak this time around, or will India extend their dominance? We shall find out.
